sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s make your code smarter! Today, you’ll learn how to make decisions in Java using `if` statements.

• How to check conditions and run code only when they’re true
• Simple syntax that’s easy to remember
• Real examples you can try right now

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you’re a traffic light. 🚦
- **Green light?** Cars go (`if` condition is true → run code).
- **Red light?** Cars stop (`if` condition is false → skip code).

`if` statements work the same way! They let your program choose what to do based on conditions.

• **Basic structure**: `if (condition) { do this }`
• **Example**: `if (age >= 18) { System.out.println("You can vote!"); }`
• **Key idea**: The code inside `{}` only runs if the condition is `true`.

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how `if` statements work:

steps.title: Check the Condition
steps.description: Java looks at the condition inside `if ( )`. Is it `true` or `false`?

steps.title: Decision Time!
steps.description: If `true`, run the code inside `{ }`. If `false`, skip it entirely.

steps.title: Move On
steps.description: After the `if` block, the program continues normally.

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Curly braces `{ }` group code to run (or skip)

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
sections.protip: Add comments like `// Check if user is an adult` to explain your `if` statements!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where are `if` statements used in real apps?

problem.description: Write a program that checks if a number is positive, negative, or zero. Print a message for each case!
hints: Use `if`, `else if`, and `else` for all 3 cases
problem.explanation: We check `number > 0` first. If false, we check `number < 0`. If both are false, the number must be zero!

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 `if` statements let your code make decisions
📌 Practice with real examples (like checking grades or ages)
